surfaces.part: right crystal spike and base cluster

answer.evidence: The object is a small cluster of pointed crystal spikes at rows 7-14, widening from 2 px at the tips to 10 px at row 12. Each column scan runs from a light tip pixel down through yellow faces to a dark base (x=6: rows 7-12, x=9: rows 9-13, x=11: rows 10-12). This is a vertical shading gradient, not a horizontal band. There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse, or visible contents. The pointed tips and the 1 px light highlight at the top of each spike are tips, not top planes. The cluster reads as a front elevation of upright crystals with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny cluster of yellow crystal spikes, far smaller than any reference prop (under one 16x16 tile), so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It has only 9 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. I see about 3 lightness steps on the crystals (a light yellow, a mid yellow and a dark base), while Beodeul props show 5-6 per material. The outline looks like a thin dark olive/brown, but the piece is too small to tell whether it is truly tinted, so I call it mixed. There is no visible grain, facet highlight or per-crystal shading, and the spikes read as flat shapes with a single dark edge, which is the sticker look. Next to the hedge, stall and well, it looks thinner and flatter. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references.

answer.evidence: Small cluster of yellow crystal shards spanning rows 7-14, widest at row 12 (10 px). Each shard is drawn only as a vertical face, so no top surface is visible. As scattered debris it is a loose pile, but it is drawn in elevation.
